title: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C)
description: Own-authored HIPAA Security Rule coverage pack: Administrative, Physical, Technical, Organizational, and Documentation safeguards for electronic protected health information (ePHI), crosswalked to the CFR citation identifiers. Control text is clean-room Caisson prose.

controls.title: Security management process and risk analysis
controls.statement: The organization runs a security management process for electronic protected health information (ePHI), beginning with an accurate and thorough risk analysis of the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the ePHI it holds.
controls.guidance: Record the risk-analysis date and scope as evidence; re-run it after material change to systems handling ePHI.

controls.title: Risk management measures
controls.statement: The organization implements security measures sufficient to reduce risks to ePHI to a reasonable and appropriate level, and tracks those measures to completion.

controls.title: Workforce sanction policy
controls.statement: A documented sanction policy applies appropriate consequences to workforce members who fail to comply with the organization's security policies and procedures.

controls.title: Assigned security responsibility and accountability
controls.statement: A named individual or role holds documented accountability for the information security program, and security responsibilities are assigned across the organization with sufficient authority and resources to execute them.

controls.title: Workforce authorization and access management
controls.statement: Access to ePHI is authorized and supervised; the organization grants, documents, reviews, and terminates each workforce member's access on the principle of minimum necessary use.

controls.title: Unique user identification
controls.statement: Each user is assigned a unique identifier so that access to and actions on ePHI are attributable to a single individual; shared or anonymous accounts for ePHI access are prohibited.

controls.title: Emergency access procedure
controls.statement: A documented and tested procedure provides necessary access to ePHI during an emergency, while preserving attribution and a record of the emergency access for later review.

controls.title: Automatic logoff of inactive sessions
controls.statement: Electronic sessions that access ePHI terminate automatically after a defined period of inactivity, reducing the risk of unauthorized access to an unattended workstation.

controls.title: Person or entity authentication
controls.statement: The organization verifies that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed before access is granted, using authentication that resists credential reuse.

controls.title: Encryption of ePHI at rest
controls.statement: ePHI maintained by the organization is encrypted at rest using a current, industry-accepted mechanism, with keys held under controlled custody so that exposure of the storage medium does not disclose plaintext ePHI.

controls.title: ePHI integrity protection
controls.statement: The organization protects ePHI from improper alteration or destruction and can detect when ePHI has been altered, both in storage and in transit.

controls.title: Transmission security for ePHI
controls.statement: ePHI transmitted over an electronic communications network is guarded against unauthorized access, including encryption of the transmission where appropriate to the risk.

controls.title: Audit controls over ePHI systems
controls.statement: Hardware, software, or procedural mechanisms record and examine activity in systems that contain or use ePHI, so that access and changes are attributable and reviewable.

crosswalk.note: Satisfied by the immutable audit log.

controls.title: Security incident procedures
controls.statement: The organization identifies and responds to suspected or known security incidents, mitigates their harmful effects to the extent practicable, and documents incidents and their outcomes.

controls.title: Contingency plan and data backup
controls.statement: A contingency plan governs response to events that damage systems containing ePHI, including a data backup plan and a disaster recovery plan that are tested and kept current.

controls.title: Facility access controls
controls.statement: Physical access to facilities and systems that house ePHI is limited to authorized personnel, while ensuring properly authorized access is allowed.

controls.title: Device and media controls
controls.statement: The receipt, removal, reuse, and disposal of hardware and electronic media that contain ePHI are governed so that ePHI is not improperly disclosed or left recoverable on decommissioned media.

controls.title: Business associate agreements
controls.statement: Before a business associate creates, receives, maintains, or transmits ePHI on the organization's behalf, a written agreement binds the associate to safeguard the ePHI to the standard the organization is itself held to.

controls.title: Policies, procedures, and documentation retention
controls.statement: Security policies and procedures are documented, and required actions, activities, and assessments are recorded and retained for the regulatory period, available to those responsible for implementing them.
controls.guidance: Retain documentation for the HIPAA six-year floor; the WORM retention helper enforces the minimum so evidence is not disposed of early.
